entries.what_happened: Three manuscripts in this family bear on BSD, with nested scope. (1) 'Exact Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank' (dated 7 Oct 2026) claims: for every E/ℚ and every prime q with s_q(E) in {0,1}, where s_q(E) is the ℤ_q-corank of the full q-power Selmer group, the algebraic rank, the analytic rank and s_q(E) all coincide, Sha(E/ℚ) is finite, and the full leading-term formula L⁽ʳ⁾(E,1)/r! = Ω_E·Reg_E·#Sha(E/ℚ)·∏_ℓ c_ℓ(E) / #E(ℚ)_tors² holds, with no hypotheses on reduction, torsion, isogeny, CM or residual representation. The rank and finiteness statements are taken from (2) and the two-primary equality from (3); the paper's own new content is the exact valuation at every odd prime, obtained from a pair identity over an auxiliary imaginary quadratic twist, a one-sided nonnegativity inequality for non-CM curves, a unit comparison, and a separate CM argument. (2) 'The Selmer converse for elliptic curves at every prime' (dated 7 Oct 2026) claims: for every E/ℚ, every prime p and r in {0,1}, s_p(E)=r implies analytic rank = Mordell–Weil rank = r and #Sha(E/ℚ) < ∞. It says nothing about the leading coefficient. Its odd-prime argument is by contradiction from an assumed torsion Heegner point, through theta series on a unitary group, cusp lifting and Galois extraction. As an application it claims that for every prime ℓ ≡ 4,7,8 (mod 9) the cubic X³+Y³=ℓZ³ has analytic and Mordell–Weil rank one and finite Sha, hence every such ℓ is a sum of two rational cubes; the text says Yin and Burungale–Tian had these cases already. (3) 'The two-primary Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer corank at most one' (dated 6 Oct 2026) claims: for E/ℚ with s_2(E) ≤ 1, rank = analytic rank = s_2(E), Sha finite, and Q_E = L⁽ʳ⁾(E,1)·(#E_tors)² / (r!·Ω_E·Reg_E·∏_ℓ c_ℓ(E)) is a positive rational with v₂(Q_E) = v₂(#Sha). Its corollary gives the same conclusions for any E with some s_p(E) ≤ 1, and a density statement: for a fixed curve, on a density-one set of signed squarefree twists, the twists have s_2 equal to 0 or 1, each value having density one half, with the two-primary formula holding for them.
entries.delivers: For curves E/ℚ with some p-Selmer corank ≤ 1, the claims cover all three parts of the list's conjecture: part (1), equality of algebraic and analytic rank; part (2), the leading-term formula; part (3), finiteness of Sha. The formula in (1) uses the list's constants with normalizations the paper states: Ω_E integrates |ω_E| over all real components of E(ℝ), with ω_E a global minimal Néron differential; c_ℓ(E) = [E(ℚ_ℓ):E₀(ℚ_ℓ)] at every finite prime; Reg_E is the determinant of B(P,Q) = (H(P+Q)−H(P)−H(Q))/2 on a basis of E(ℚ)/torsion, with H(P) = lim 4^(−n) log max(|a|,b) for x(2ⁿP) = a/b, which is the canonical height attached to 2[O] (twice the one attached to [O]); Reg_E = 1 in rank 0, and an index-m sublattice multiplies it by m². L(E,s) is the full Hasse–Weil L-function with its bad Euler factors. The list does not fix these conventions, so the match holds under the paper's stated ones. Scope: the covered class is curves with some s_p ≤ 1 at some prime p. Since s_p(E) ≥ rank E(ℚ) for every p, by the Kummer sequence, no curve of rank ≥ 2 is covered. Manuscript (3) by itself proves only the 2-primary part. Each twist in its density-one set has s_2 ≤ 1, so manuscript (1) applies to each, which would give the full formula on that set; neither manuscript states this combination.
entries.remains: Curves E/ℚ whose p-Selmer coranks are all ≥ 2 are untouched by all three manuscripts. This includes every curve of Mordell–Weil rank ≥ 2. For these, rank equality, the leading-term formula and finiteness of Sha all remain open. Among curves of rank 0 or 1, those with s_p ≥ 2 for every prime p also remain open. Not addressed: the number-field form given in the Wikipedia lead, and the abelian-variety form in the Clay statement. Within the covered class the text claims nothing remains.
entries.direction: proves the full conjecture (all three parts, with the list's constants) for the subclass of curves with some p-Selmer corank ≤ 1; the two-primary manuscript proves only the 2-primary part of the leading term
entries.conditional_on: Manuscript (1) takes rank and finiteness from manuscript (2) and the two-primary equality from manuscript (3). Those are separate manuscripts of this family and (1) does not prove them. Manuscripts (1), (2) and (3) choose their auxiliary imaginary quadratic fields with the twist-density theorem of 'Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves' (OpenAI); manuscript (2) also takes its p = 2 case from that manuscript, and (3) uses the proof of its Theorem 1.2 for the density corollary. The CM case of (1) uses Burungale–Flach's exact BSD theorem for CM curves with nonvanishing L-value at 1 (their Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1), applied after an isogeny. The CM comparison in (3) uses Burungale–Flach's machinery (their Proposition 3.1, Theorem 4.1 and Proposition 4.1) and Kato's reciprocity law. Classical inputs include Gross–Zagier, Kolyvagin, modularity, and Cassels–Milne isogeny invariance.
entries.doubts: The texts flag no step as sketched and state no hedges. Points bearing on trust: (a) The odd-prime argument of (1), in its Sections 5 to 9, is the bulk of the paper. I read only its introduction, Section 2 and the assembly in Section 10, not those proofs. The introduction names the passage from an integral quotient to an exact unit at the central point, by theta constructions with growing p-level and removal of quotient divisors by added tame variables, as the step that makes the central comparison exact. (b) The rank-zero CM lemma in (1) is short. It asserts that after an isogeny the Burungale–Flach hypotheses hold, says the non-maximal-order case is supplied by a preceding lattice argument, and cites the descent step to Burungale–Flach Corollary 2. (c) The CM leading-coefficient corollary in (3) is condensed. It says the same calculation 'in the period-normalized sense' gives the claim, and handles elements needing denominators by passing to a multiple and 'homogeneity'. (d) The density corollary in (3) takes its Selmer-corank input from the proof, not the stated form, of Theorem 1.2 of the Goldfeld manuscript, whose stated theorem is about analytic rank.

entries.what_happened: None of the three manuscripts mentions congruent numbers, Tunnell's theorem or rational right triangles. The bearing is indirect, through 'The Selmer converse for elliptic curves at every prime'. For squarefree n > 0, the congruent-number curve is E_n: y² = x³ − n²x, and n is congruent exactly when rank E_n(ℚ) ≥ 1. That manuscript's theorem gives rank E_n(ℚ) = s_p(E_n) whenever some p-Selmer corank s_p(E_n) is ≤ 1. The manuscripts do not draw this consequence. The sum-of-two-cubes corollary in the same manuscript concerns X³+Y³=ℓZ³ and not congruent numbers, so the matching note's stated reason does not supply the bearing; the bearing is the rank statement above. 'Exact Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank' also covers E_n whenever some s_q(E_n) ≤ 1, with the full leading-term formula, but does not mention congruent numbers or Tunnell's criterion.
entries.delivers: No determination of congruent numbers is claimed. The consequence the Selmer converse yields, which the text does not state: for each squarefree n for which some Selmer corank of E_n is ≤ 1, n is congruent if and only if that corank equals 1. A corank of 0 shows n is not congruent; a corank of 1 shows it is. This decides only those n, through a Selmer-based test that requires the coranks to be computed. It gives nothing for an n whose Selmer coranks are all ≥ 2. The problem's request for a precise characterisation is not met, and no Tunnell-type criterion appears in the manuscripts.
entries.remains: For n whose E_n has every p-Selmer corank ≥ 2 (this includes every n whose E_n has rank ≥ 2), these results leave open whether n is congruent. The characterisation for all n is not given. Whether the determination is unconditional is open in the sense that it depends on the Goldfeld manuscript (see conditional_on). The text does not discuss the literal wording 'rational numbers' against squarefree integers; E_n depends on n only up to squares over ℚ, so the reduction to squarefree n is harmless but unstated.
entries.direction: partial Selmer-based criterion: the rank of E_n equals a p-Selmer corank whenever that corank is ≤ 1; no full characterisation
entries.conditional_on: The implication rests on 'The Selmer converse for elliptic curves at every prime', which at p = 2 and for its auxiliary-field choice depends on 'Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves' (OpenAI, Theorems 1.1 and 1.2). That manuscript is not among the files I read, so I have not checked it.
entries.doubts: The congruent-number implication is my deduction from the Selmer converse's theorem. No manuscript states it, and none checks the translation to individual n. The matching note's reason (sum of two cubes) is a statement about X³+Y³=ℓZ³, not about congruent numbers. No manuscript computes any Selmer corank of an E_n.
